NC — NEG CASE
Framework
V: Justice
VC: Fulfilling existing moral duties
Moral imperative requires an actual duty.
Nussbaum: justice requires securing basic capabilities necessary for human dignity.
Beneficial ≠ morally required.
C1 — Existing Moral Duties
Concrete suffering exists now: poverty, disease, displacement, lack of healthcare/education.
Humanity has existing duties to people whose basic capabilities are being denied.
Future people matter, but future benefits don't automatically override existing duties.
Aff must prove colonization specifically is necessary.
C2 — Exploration ≠ Colonization
Scientific research ≠ permanent settlement.
Satellites/probes/telescopes/ISS provide benefits without colonies.
DART demonstrates planetary defense without colonization.
Aff must prove necessity of colonization, not just usefulness of space.
1AR — AFF RESPONSES
Framework
V: Life
VC: Prevent human extinction
Humans cannot flourish if they don't exist.
Claims Aff framework supports Neg because survival is prerequisite to flourishing.
C1 Responses
Neg is “fixated on short term.”
Today's people may be dead in the future.
Need to prioritize extinction prevention.
Claims zero demonstrated tradeoff between colonization and helping people today.
“People today are future people.”
C2 Responses
Says Aff isn't relying on exploration arguments.
Space provides medical research/technology.
Earth's risks are unique and won't necessarily exist on other planets.
Other Aff Arguments
99.9% of species have gone extinct.
Bostrom: technological development creates existential risks.
WMDs could cause extinction.
“Try or die”: Aff doesn't need to prove colonization always works.
NASA technology makes colonization feasible.
Different planetary compositions/resources provide additional benefits.

"New AFFs" are affirmatives that have not been read by you, a teammate, your prep group, or another school. To be read as 'new,' none of the evidence in the AFF should have been read before. If evidence has been read before, the evidence should be disclosed to your opponent. Changing tags/how a card is cut does not make an affirmative new.

Average varsity LD experience
average K debater — changes the ROB every 3 minutes, goes for framework every round, does not actually care, never criticizes NSDA and the cost of going to tournaments.
average theory debater — has not researched the topic since September but knows 46 reasons disclosure is a voter

average tricks debater — “they have dropped indexicals from the 1ac and it is not a trick or apriori”
average K aff — resolution? never heard of; hate debate although we are actively spending money in it
average topicality debater — spends six minutes debating what “the” means
average disclosure debater — knows your entire competitive history before knowing your name
average doc — 43 pages, 38 are unread, 4 are hidden in 2-point font, one sentence apparently decides the round
average card — tag says EXTINCTION INEVITABLE, actual author says “further research may be warranted”
average highlight — 97% of the warrant mysteriously disappeared
average evidence ethics — “it was in the card bro trust”
average CX — asks a question, interrupts the answer, later says you conceded; never answers a single question directly
average 1AR — 4 minutes claims without warrants cuz it's impossible
average 2NR — “judge, this round is actually incredibly simple”
average 2AR — explains why the incredibly simple round has 19 layers
average judge — “I was persuaded by an argument neither debater went for”
average debater — doc bots, wiki stalking, doing anything to win while actively claiming they are fair and educational, tiny-font qualifications, hidden analytics, and seventeen ways to win without ever discussing the topic
